newsitem.title: UK: Air UK does not renew Bridges cargo contra.
newsitem.headline: Air UK does not renew Bridges cargo contra.

text.p: Air UK said that an arrangement under which London-based express courier company Bridges Worldwide managed its cargo operations had ceased with immediate effect.
A spokeswoman for Air UK, 45 percent owned by Dutch carrier KLM, said that the one-year agreement with Bridges would not be renewed, without elaborating.

A statement issued by the London Stansted Airport-based airline to all managers and staff said that "a number of alternative options are currently being considered as to the future management of the cargo function".
It added that in the interim period, Air UK intended to take back its cargo operations in-house, which was the situation prior to the contract being signed with Bridges Worldwide.
The statement said that Allan McQuarrie had been appointed acting cargo manager.
No comment was immediately available from Bridges Worldwide.

The outsourcing agreement with Bridges was concluded after Air UK's former cargo manager Kevin Durnin left the carrier at the beginning of 1996 to set up his own cargo management company, Viking Freight Services.
